'''Raphael Bousso''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|b|uː|s|oʊ}}) (born 1971) is a [[theoretical physicist]] and [[cosmologist]]. He is a professor at [[UC Berkeley]], where he holds the Chancellor's Chair in Physics. He is known for the [[Bousso's holographic bound|Bousso bound]] on the information content of the universe.<ref name="CEC">{{cite journal

}}</ref><ref name="HGS">{{cite journal

}}
</ref><ref>

==Life and career==
Bousso was born in [[Haifa]], Israel, the son of late scientist {{ill|Dino Bousso|qid=Q133871705|s=1|v=sup}}.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.netsivi.org/bousso.htm|title=In Memory of Dino Bousso (1933-1971)|access-date=11 October 2020}}</ref> He grew up near [[Augsburg]], Germany,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bousso group members|url=https://lightsheet.berkeley.edu/members/|access-date=2020-10-10}}</ref> where he studied physics from 1990 until 1993. Bousso earned his [[PhD|Ph.D.]] at [[Cambridge University]] in 1997; his doctoral advisor was [[Stephen Hawking]]. Bousso did [[postdoctoral research]] at [[Stanford University]] until 2000, and at the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in Santa Barbara until 2002. In 2002/03, Bousso was a fellow at the [[Harvard University]] physics department and the [[Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study]]. Since 2002, he has been a professor in the physics department at the [[UC Berkeley|University of California, Berkeley]]. In 2012, Bousso was elected Fellow of the American Physical Society "for fundamental discoveries in the field of quantum cosmology, including the covariant entropy bound and the string landscape."<ref>{{Cite web|title = APS Fellowship 2012 |url = https://www.aps.org/units/dpf/fellowship/index.cfm?year=2012}}</ref> In 2026, he was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2026 New Member List {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2026 |access-date=2026-04-25 |website=www.amacad.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Research==
Bousso's research is focused on [[quantum gravity]] and [[cosmology]], particularly through the study of [[quantum information]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bousso Group|url=https://lightsheet.berkeley.edu/|access-date=2010-11-13}}</ref> His 1999 covariant entropy bound<ref name="CEC" /> ([[Bousso's holographic bound|Bousso bound]]) established a general relation between quantum information and the geometry of spacetime (i.e., [[General relativity|gravity]]).<ref>{{Cite web|title = The Holographic Principle |website = [[Scientific American]] |url = https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/sidebar-the-holographic-p/ |access-date = 2018-08-27}}</ref> The Bousso bound has since been refined and strengthened, leading to provable new results in quantum field theory, such as the quantum null energy condition.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Proof of a Quantum Bousso Bound|url=http://inspirehep.net/record/1291932?ln=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Proof of the Quantum Null Energy Condition|url=http://inspirehep.net/record/1392634?ln=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=A General Proof of the Quantum Null Energy Condition|url=http://inspirehep.net/record/1608046?ln=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Black Holes, Quantum Information, and Unification|url=https://calendar.mit.edu/event/physics_colloquium_raphael_bousso#.W4QWLi2ZM1I|access-date=2018-08-27}}</ref> Bousso has also worked on the [[black hole information paradox]] (firewall problem).<ref>{{Cite news|title=A Black Hole Mystery Wrapped in a Firewall Paradox, New York Times, August 13, 2013|work=The New York Times |date=12 August 2013 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/08/13/science/space/a-black-hole-mystery-wrapped-in-a-firewall-paradox.html|access-date=2018-08-27 |last1=Overbye |first1=Dennis }}</ref> Since 2018, he has led a consortium of theoretical and experimental physicists exploring and developing the relations between quantum gravity, quantum information, and quantum computing.<ref>{{Cite web|title=GeoFlow Award|url=https://www.orau.gov/qispi2018/abstracts/Cosmos-and-Quibits-Abstracts.pdf|access-date=October 10, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=geoflow|url=https://sites.google.com/view/geoflow/home|access-date=2020-10-11|website=sites.google.com|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2000, Bousso and [[Joseph Polchinski]] argued that [[string theory]] has many long-lived [[Vacuum solution|vacua]], including solutions compatible with the observed positive value of the [[cosmological constant]] ([[vacuum energy]]).<ref name = "BP" /> This came to be called the "landscape of string theory."<ref>L. Susskind, "The anthropic landscape of string theory", {{arxiv|hep-th/0302219}}.</ref><ref name = "SA" /> Bousso has developed an approach to the cosmological measure problem,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bousso|first=Raphael|date=2006-11-06|title=Holographic probabilities in eternal inflation|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=97|issue=19|article-number=191302|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.97.191302|pmid=17155610|arxiv=hep-th/0605263|bibcode=2006PhRvL..97s1302B |s2cid=977375 |issn=0031-9007}}</ref> with the ultimate goal of testing the string theory landscape.<ref>{{Cite web|title = A geometric solution to the coincidence problem, and the size of the landscape as the origin of hierarchy |url = http://inspirehep.net/record/875183?ln=en}}</ref>
